headline: UPS beats, futures edge up before the Fed; bitcoin steadies near $79,800
summary: Wall Street closed higher Monday on a chip and Tesla rebound (S&P 500 +0.7% to 7,677, Nasdaq +0.8%, TSX +0.4% to 35,944), and U.S. futures are slightly higher early Tuesday as the Fed opens its two-day meeting, with UPS up about 1% before the bell after beating forecasts and raising its outlook. Crypto has steadied: bitcoin is about $79,800 (down 0.4% over 24 hours) after U.S. bitcoin ETFs took in about $110 million Monday, ether is about $2,312, total crypto value is about $2.66 trillion and Fear & Greed sits at a neutral 48. U.S. crude has eased about 1% to near $101, gold is about $4,026, the 10-year yield is just under 5%, and markets price about a 90% chance the Fed holds on Wednesday, the same day the Bank of Canada is expected to hike.

crypto.label: Cautious
crypto.why: Bitcoin is pinned just under $80,000 with Fear & Greed at a neutral 48; Monday's small bitcoin ETF inflow broke a two-day outflow streak, but ether ETFs are still losing money and Strategy has paused buying.

stocks.label: Risk-on
stocks.why: The Nasdaq rose 0.8% Monday, the VIX has eased to about 17.8 and futures are slightly higher after UPS beat, but a 10-year yield near 5% and Wednesday's Fed, Bank of Canada and big-tech earnings keep the rally on a short leash.

drivers.title: Chips lead a broad tech rally as Meta sells stock
drivers.detail: Meta launched a $35 billion stock sale to fund AI spending, and Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom may buy up to $5 billion of it, per AP; AMD (+2.8%), Nvidia (+2.4%) and Broadcom (+2.3%) led Monday's rebound while Meta fell 1.9% to about $631. Asia followed Tuesday, with South Korea's KOSPI up 3.1% and Japan's Nikkei up 1.7%, per AP, and memory names Micron, SanDisk and SK Hynix were rising in U.S. premarket trade after reports SK Hynix may pay a special dividend of about $12 billion, per TipRanks.

crypto.name: Bitcoin
crypto.move: Down 0.4% over 24h and down 1.9% this week, at about $79,800 (down 5.9% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Bitcoin slipped under $80,000 in Asian trading Monday as traders cut risk before Wednesday's Fed decision and has hovered just below it since, ticking up to about $79,800 early Tuesday. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs (funds that hold the coin for stock-market investors) took in about $110 million Monday, per SoSoValue data cited by CoinGabbar, after roughly $943 million of outflows over the prior three sessions per Farside, but Strategy said it made no bitcoin purchases in the week to Oct. 25, per Investing.com. A wallet tied to miner MARA also sent nearly 1,000 BTC to Galaxy Digital, per The Crypto Times, while futures markets price about a 90% chance the Fed holds rates.
crypto.meaning: Glassnode estimates ETF buyers and corporate treasuries bought, on average, between about $80,000 and $81,500, so bitcoin is sitting right around the price where many big holders break even; staying under it can prompt more selling. Monday's ETF inflow is a modest first sign that dip buyers are returning, but one day is not a trend.

outlook.bullCase: A calm Fed on Oct. 28, ETF inflows returning and a U.S.–Iran deal could lift it back above $82,000–$82,500 (Thursday's lost floor), putting $85,000–$87,000 back in view.
outlook.bearCase: A daily close below $79,000, more ETF outflows, a hawkish Fed or a U.S. strike on Iran could extend the slide toward $77,600 (Glassnode's estimate of the average holder's cost) and then $75,000.
outlook.watch: Whether it can close back above $80,000, whether ETF inflows continue, the Fed decision and Warsh press conference on Oct. 28, whether Strategy resumes buying (its results are Oct. 29), and about $11 billion of bitcoin options expiring Oct. 30.

crypto.name: Ethereum
crypto.move: Down 0.5% over 24h and down 2.8% this week, at about $2,312 (down 14.8% over 30 days)

It is still under the $2,400 level that had supported it for about a week, and ether ETFs lost another roughly $89 million Monday, led by BlackRock's fund, per SoSoValue data cited by CoinGabbar, even as bitcoin ETFs drew money back in.
crypto.meaning: Ether is lagging bitcoin because big investors keep pulling money from the ETFs. Until those flows turn, rallies may be harder to sustain.

outlook.bullCase: Climbing back above $2,400, with ETF outflows stopping, could open a move toward $2,500 and then about $2,700, where October began.
outlook.bearCase: A break below $2,290 (Saturday's low) with continued ETF outflows and more forced selling could send it toward $2,150–$2,200, and a broader risk-off turn could push it lower.
outlook.watch: Daily ether ETF flows, the $2,300 and $2,400 levels, the ETH/BTC ratio, and any new Glamsterdam upgrade timeline.

crypto.name: Quack AI
crypto.move: About $0.071, still up 27.5% over 24h on our feed but down roughly 50% from about $0.147 at 5 a.m. ET and about 65% below Monday's peak near $0.20
crypto.why: Quack AI pitches itself as an AI layer for crypto governance, using software agents to read and vote on project proposals; its Q token runs on BNB Chain and Ethereum. It spiked about 260% to roughly $0.20 Monday with no official news, and a report via Pluang said about 78% of roughly $280 million in trading volume looked like wash trading (the same parties buying and selling to fake activity), with two wallets holding about 1.7% of supply accumulating for weeks. Early Tuesday the spike unravelled fast, with the price falling from about $0.147 to the low $0.08s within about an hour on our feed and drifting lower to about $0.071 since, again with no announcement; it has also slipped out of CoinGecko's top 100 to about No. 133.
crypto.meaning: This is the typical pattern of a coordinated pump in a thinly traded token: a fast spike with no news, then a fast collapse that leaves late buyers with big losses. A mintable contract (more tokens can be created) and a possible unlock of roughly 225–249 million Q around Nov. 2, which Quack AI's own schedule does not confirm, add dilution risk.

outlook.bullCase: If buyers step in around $0.07 and the token stabilizes, a bounce toward $0.09–$0.10 is possible, though moves this violent rarely retrace cleanly.
outlook.bearCase: If selling continues, Q could fall back toward about $0.06 or below, roughly where it sat before Monday's spike, with the possible Nov. 2 unlock adding pressure.
outlook.watch: Whether $0.07 holds, transfers from the top wallets to exchanges, futures funding and open interest, and any confirmation of the Nov. 2 unlock.

crypto.name: Bitway
crypto.move: Down 4.3% over 24h and down 19.0% this week, at about $1.46 (up 22.5% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Bitway remains one of the worst performers in CoinGecko's top 100 today, with no specific news trigger we could find; it had already fallen about 25% on Oct. 15 when a hot U.S. inflation report hit crypto, and slid from above $2.60 to about $1.70 in the week to Oct. 24, per CoinMarketCap's update page. Trackers say the top 100 wallets hold almost all of the supply, which makes sharp moves like this more likely, and about 101.6 million BTW (roughly 1% of the 10 billion total, about $138 million at today's price) is due to unlock on Nov. 2, per CryptoTicker. An unlock is when tokens held back for insiders or ecosystem funds become free to sell. An early-afternoon bounce of nearly 30% off a low near $1.00 has mostly faded, typical of a thinly traded token after a crash, again with no news we could find.
crypto.meaning: This is a high-risk token whose price can swing tens of percent in a day, with conflicting public data on how many tokens are actually circulating. Holders face more supply coming each month through 2030, and whether the Nov. 2 tranche goes to early backers (more likely to sell) or ecosystem pools is disputed between trackers.

outlook.bullCase: If selling exhausts near $1.00 and the market absorbs the Nov. 2 unlock without a fresh drop, a rebound toward $1.40–$1.70 (last week's levels) is possible.
outlook.bearCase: If large holders keep selling into thin trading, a break below $1.00 could open a slide toward $0.80, especially around the Nov. 2 unlock.
outlook.watch: Whether $1.00 holds, large wallet transfers to exchanges, trading volume, and price action around the Nov. 2 08:00 UTC unlock.

crypto.name: LayerZero
crypto.move: Down 1.5% over 24h and down 14.2% this week, at about $1.66 (roughly flat over 30 days)
crypto.why: LayerZero runs a messaging system that lets apps send tokens and data between different blockchains, and ZRO is its token. It is one of the worst performers in the top 100 today, but we found no fresh headline behind Monday's drop. It has been weak since an Oct. 20 token unlock (about 6% of supply), after which roughly 9.7 million ZRO was reportedly moved to big exchanges, per CoinMarketCap's AI news summary; an unlock is when tokens held back for insiders become free to sell. The project announced on Oct. 20 that its Zero mainnet and lzATLAS launch, which adds a buy-and-burn of ZRO funded by fees, is planned for Nov. 30, per TokenPost.
crypto.meaning: Recurring unlocks keep adding supply that early holders can sell, which has outweighed upgrade news so far this month. The Nov. 30 launch is the project's main potential catalyst, but a fee-funded burn only helps the price if the network earns meaningful fees.

outlook.bullCase: If selling from the unlock runs out and bitcoin steadies above $80,000, ZRO could bounce back toward $1.80–$2.00, where it traded last week.
outlook.bearCase: Continued exchange deposits from large wallets or a weaker crypto market after the Fed could push it below $1.60 toward about $1.40–$1.50.
outlook.watch: Large ZRO transfers to exchanges, whether $1.60 holds, the next monthly unlock date, and any update on the Nov. 30 Zero mainnet launch.

crypto.name: XRP
crypto.move: Up 1.3% over 24h and up 0.7% this week, at about $1.30 (down 15.4% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Ripple, the company most closely tied to XRP, won final approval from the U.S. bank regulator (the OCC) for a national trust bank that will manage the reserves behind its RLUSD stablecoin and hold crypto for institutional clients, per CoinDesk. XRP rose about 1% on the news, per Investing.com, but is still around $1.30. Separately, Franklin Templeton last week put about $150 million more of its tokenized money-market fund onto the XRP Ledger, per CoinDesk.
crypto.meaning: A federal bank charter gives Ripple's stablecoin and custody business more credibility with banks, but neither the charter nor tokenized funds require anyone to buy XRP, so the price link is indirect. XRP is still down about 15% over the past month, so this is a small bounce inside a larger slide.

outlook.bullCase: More tokenized-fund news and a steadier bitcoin above $80,000 could lift XRP back toward $1.40–$1.45.
outlook.bearCase: If bitcoin loses $80,000 again or the wider market turns risk-off after the Fed, XRP could slip back toward $1.20–$1.25.
outlook.watch: Whether XRP can hold gains on the bank-charter news, RLUSD growth, bitcoin's hold on $80,000, and the Oct. 28 Fed decision.

crypto.name: Quant
crypto.move: Down 4.6% over 24h but up 6.3% this week, at about $204 (up 19.1% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Quant makes software (its Overledger platform) that lets banks move tokenized money, meaning bank deposits recorded on a blockchain-style ledger, between different systems. The token is up about 17% over the past month, helped by news that The Clearing House, the payments company owned by big U.S. banks, picked Quant's technology in late September for a project to settle tokenized deposits over its existing payment rails, with rollout targeted for the first half of 2027; seven big UK banks also made the first live customer payments with tokenized sterling on infrastructure Quant built, per CoinMarketCap. It jumped about 7% Monday without a fresh announcement we could find and has given back about 4% over 24 hours by early Tuesday, while still trending on CoinGecko.
crypto.meaning: QNT is trading on a real business story, bank adoption of tokenized money, rather than pure hype, but the actual rollout is still more than six months away and banks paying for software does not automatically mean demand for the token. After a roughly 21% gain in a month, much of the good news may already be in the price.

outlook.bullCase: More bank or payments-network announcements, or a broader recovery in crypto, could carry it past about $210–$225 on continued momentum.
outlook.bearCase: Profit-taking after a strong month, or a wider crypto sell-off if bitcoin stays below $80,000, could pull it back toward the $175–$180 area or lower.
outlook.watch: Any new partnership news from The Clearing House or UK banks, whether trading volume stays high, and bitcoin's direction around the Fed decision.

crypto.name: MemeCore
crypto.move: Up 1.1% over 24h and up 26.5% this week, at about $1.01 (down 18.0% over 30 days)
crypto.why: MemeCore, a blockchain built around meme coins, was the biggest decliner among about 90 large coins tracked by TokenPost on Sunday morning, falling to about $0.92; it has since bounced to about $0.99, roughly flat over 24 hours, with no specific trigger reported either way. The swings follow a choppy month: the token fell about 23% in the week to Oct. 19 after LayerZero and Stargate opened bridges letting holders move M to BNB Chain and Base, then bounced roughly 50%. On-chain investigator ZachXBT has previously accused insiders of manipulating the token's price, and a token unlock is due Nov. 1.
crypto.meaning: Moves of 20% in a day without clear news are typical of tokens where a few wallets hold much of the supply, so price can swing on a handful of trades. About 56 million new M tokens (roughly 2.8% of circulating supply, about $50 million, per CoinDesk) unlock on Nov. 1, which adds potential selling pressure.

outlook.bullCase: If the sell-off was one large holder exiting and the broader market steadies, it could rebound toward $1.05–$1.15, where it traded earlier this week.
outlook.bearCase: More large-wallet selling or selling ahead of the Nov. 1 unlock could push it toward $0.75–$0.80, its lows from mid-October.
outlook.watch: Large transfers to exchanges from top wallets, the Nov. 1 unlock, and whether the project explains the drop.

crypto.name: Zcash
crypto.move: Up 2.4% over 24h and up 10.9% this week, at about $1,252 (down 24.6% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Traders had been positioning for the NU7 upgrade, which developers scheduled for about 7:50 p.m. ET on Nov. 5; it cuts block times from 75 to 25 seconds and sends 60% of fees to a reserve. Futures open interest (the value of open bets) had risen about 19–24% and two large traders reportedly opened about $37.6 million of 10x leveraged longs. Those leveraged bets have been unwinding: CoinDesk flagged ZEC among the coins where bullish traders were closing positions, and it noted an 8% drop in open interest Friday. After dipping below the $1,190–$1,230 support area, the price has bounced back to about $1,241 (up about 1% over 24 hours), inside the top of that zone.
crypto.meaning: Much of this month's rally was driven by borrowed money, and this week shows how fast that can reverse. Upgrade dates often bring 'buy the rumour, sell the news' behaviour, so swings both ways are likely into Nov. 5.

outlook.bullCase: Holding the $1,180–$1,200 area and renewed interest as the upgrade nears could bring it back to the $1,375 resistance and, beyond that, the September high near $1,700.
outlook.bearCase: Losing $1,180 would erase the October breakout and could send it toward about $1,000–$1,120, near its 50-day average.
outlook.watch: The $1,180 level, funding rates and open interest, ETF flows, and any upgrade delay.

crypto.name: Solana
crypto.move: Down 1.2% over 24h and down 3.8% this week, at about $99.95 (down 19.6% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Solana completed its Alpenglow upgrade, a major overhaul aimed at much faster transaction finality (the point at which a payment can't be reversed), according to CoinDesk. The price has moved with the market rather than rallying on the news, and it slipped under $100 Saturday morning as bitcoin's break below $80,000 triggered forced selling across crypto, briefly tested $100 again in Asian trading Monday, and it is about $99.21 early Tuesday, just below that line.
crypto.meaning: A smooth Alpenglow launch is a meaningful technical milestone, but the market is treating it as already expected. The first days after a big upgrade are when problems usually show up, so stability matters more than headlines.

outlook.bullCase: A trouble-free upgrade and stronger crypto risk appetite could lift SOL back toward $115–$120.
outlook.bearCase: Any outage or bug after the upgrade, or bitcoin staying below $80,000, could push SOL toward $90.
outlook.watch: Whether SOL regains $100, network stability after Alpenglow, bitcoin's $80,000 level, and Solana ETF flows.

stocks.name: Celestica
stocks.move: U.S.-listed shares rose about 13% after hours Monday on results (Toronto shares trade again Tuesday; our live feed does not track CLS)
stocks.why: Celestica, a Toronto-based company that builds servers, networking switches and other hardware for AI data centres, reported third-quarter revenue of $5.83 billion, up 83% from a year earlier, and adjusted earnings of $3.30 a share, above its own guidance, per its filing. It raised its 2026 forecast to $21.0 billion of revenue and $11.55 a share (from $20.5 billion and $11.30), and gave a first 2027 outlook of $40 billion of revenue and $21.50 a share, nearly double this year. One soft spot: it cut its 2026 free-cash-flow forecast to $460 million from $600 million as it spends more to expand capacity.
stocks.meaning: The 2027 forecast says Celestica's biggest customers (large cloud companies) expect to keep spending heavily on AI hardware next year, a counterpoint to last week's worries about AI returns. The stock has already run up a lot on this story, so expectations are high and it is very sensitive to any sign that AI spending is slowing.

outlook.bullCase: If the after-hours gain holds through Tuesday's open and Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon confirm big AI spending plans this week, the stock could push toward fresh highs.
outlook.bearCase: If the broader AI-chip sell-off resumes, or investors focus on the lower cash-flow forecast and heavy spending, the early pop could fade back toward Monday's close.
outlook.watch: Where it opens Tuesday in Toronto and New York, management's comments on customer concentration and capacity, and Big Tech capital-spending guidance on Oct. 28–29.

stocks.name: Meta Platforms
stocks.move: Closed down 1.9% at about $631, near the day's low of $628; down about 10% since Wednesday
stocks.why: Meta launched a $35 billion share sale Monday to pay for AI data centres: about $22.5 billion of common stock sold through forward agreements and $12.5 billion of three-year mandatory convertible preferred shares (which turn into common stock later), plus a planned program of up to $60 billion of non-voting Class C shares starting in early 2027, per ZeroHedge and KuCoin News. Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom indicated interest in buying up to $5 billion. Shares rose before the bell, fell to about $629 after the open, recovered to about $648, before closing near the day's low at about $631. Last week's results beat forecasts, but the $135–$145 billion spending plan, roughly -$2.1 billion of free cash flow and a $9.9 billion legal charge sank the stock 7% Thursday.
stocks.meaning: Selling new shares spreads the company's profits over more stock (dilution), and the scale here is unusual for a company that was buying back shares. Chip-maker interest shows suppliers want to keep Meta spending, but it also feeds 'circular financing' worries, where AI buyers and sellers fund each other.

outlook.bullCase: If the offering is absorbed smoothly and investors refocus on 26% revenue growth, it could recover toward $680–$700.
outlook.bearCase: Pressure from new supply, rising credit-risk pricing (its five-year credit default swaps are about double August's level, per ZeroHedge) or weak results from other Big Tech spenders could push it below $630 toward $600.
outlook.watch: The offering's final pricing, whether $630 holds, and Alphabet's and Microsoft's spending plans on Oct. 28.

stocks.name: UPS
stocks.move: Up about 1.3% before the bell after its results, per Reuters (our live feed does not track UPS)
stocks.why: UPS earned an adjusted $1.69 a share last quarter, down from $1.74 a year ago but above the roughly $1.63 analysts expected, per Reuters. It raised its 2026 forecast to about $7.28 a share in adjusted profit and $92.6 billion in revenue, helped by more higher-paying international air shipments and fewer low-margin Amazon parcels, and said it is on track for $3 billion in cost savings this year.
stocks.meaning: UPS's plan to shed lower-paying volume and cut costs is showing up in margins, which had been the main worry. Because parcel volumes track spending, the results are also a mildly reassuring read on consumers and global trade.

outlook.bullCase: If the premarket gain holds and analysts lift targets after the raised outlook, the stock could build on the move as investors bet the turnaround is working.
outlook.bearCase: If investors focus on lower year-over-year profit, or tariffs and oil near $100 hit shipping demand and fuel costs, the early gain could fade.
outlook.watch: How the stock closes Tuesday, analyst target changes, fuel costs with oil near $100, and FedEx's tone at upcoming events.
